reason: H0 only passes raw bytes to the C parsing entry points plist_from_bin, plist_from_json, plist_from_openstep, and plist_from_xml, then calls plist_free. It never invokes the C++ assignment operators or constructs the aliasing state where the source and destination are the same object. S1 explicitly handles that state with `if (this == &...) return *this;` across scalar and container node classes, making C++ object assignment and self-assignment a material fuzz-worthy surface absent from H0.
evidence: fuzz/bplist_fuzzer.cc calls only plist_from_bin and plist_free.
fuzz/jplist_fuzzer.cc calls only plist_from_json and plist_free.
fuzz/oplist_fuzzer.cc calls only plist_from_openstep and plist_free.
fuzz/xplist_fuzzer.cc calls only plist_from_xml and plist_free.
Array::operator= now tests `this == &a` before plist_free, deletion of `_array` elements, plist_copy, and array_fill.
Dictionary::operator= now tests `this == &d` before clearing `_map`, copying the plist, and calling dictionary_fill.

Boolean::operator=, Data::operator=, Date::operator=, Integer::operator=, Key::operator=, Real::operator=, String::operator=, and Uid::operator= each add an explicit self-assignment identity check before freeing and copying `_node`.
recommended_action: Add a C++ API fuzz target that derives node values from fuzz input and exercises copy construction, assignment between distinct compatible objects, repeated assignment, and explicit self-assignment (`obj = obj`) for Array, Dictionary, Boolean, Data, Date, Integer, Key, Real, String, and Uid; include nested Array and Dictionary values and verify that objects remain usable and destructible after each operation under memory sanitizers.
